title: Settlement Worksheet — Net Energy Metering Move-Out Payout and Surrendered Amount
content:
This worksheet fixes the move-out payout and the surrendered amount when a Net Energy Metering agreement ends because the customer stops electric service at the address.

## Inputs

| Input | Value |
|---|---|
| Bank | The credit bank balance recorded on the agreement when the termination is recorded |
| Average monthly offsettable charges | The energy charge plus the Power Supply Cost Recovery charge of the most recent service bill of the hosting service agreement |
| Full-value months | 0.5 months |
| Tenure months | None |
| Surplus share | 1 |
| Staying uplift | None |
| Holdback share | 0 |

## The calculation

1. **Full-value limit**: the average monthly offsettable charges multiplied by the sum of the full-value months and the tenure months, rounded to the cent.
2. **Full-value portion**: the lesser of the bank and the full-value limit.
3. **Surplus**: the bank less the full-value portion.
4. **Paid surplus**: the surplus multiplied by the sum of the surplus share and the staying uplift, rounded to the cent.
5. **Estimated-read holdback**: the export credit of the most recent billing period in the net metering history multiplied by the holdback share, rounded to the cent.
6. **Move-out payout**: the full-value portion plus the paid surplus less the estimated-read holdback, rounded to the cent.
7. **Surrendered amount**: the bank less the move-out payout.

## Hypothetical worked figure

Hypothetical inputs: a bank of 612.40; a most recent service bill with an energy charge of 74.18 and a Power Supply Cost Recovery charge of 3.02.

- Average monthly offsettable charges: 77.20.
- Full-value limit: 77.20 multiplied by 0.5, that is 38.60; full-value portion 38.60.
- Surplus: 612.40 less 38.60, that is 573.80; paid surplus 573.80 multiplied by 1, that is 573.80.
- Holdback: 0.00.
- Move-out payout: 38.60 plus 573.80, that is 612.40; surrendered amount 0.00.

A bank smaller than the full-value limit is taken in full as the full-value portion, and the surplus is then zero.
